01 / Method & sources

Test pairs, not isolated colors

A color can work on one background and fail on another. Record each color's role, the ratio of solid pairs, and non-color cues for important states.

02 / Tools

Two color workbenches

Codes and results are processed in your browser; values are not sent to a Vijeron server.

01 / WCAG

Contrast checker

Calculate text and background ratio and compare it with WCAG AA thresholds for normal and large text.

03 / Guides

Eight guides from code to final review

Each guide offers a concrete example, a pitfall and primary standard references.

01 / 08

Read HEX codes and RGB channels

Understand the numbers before assigning colors to text, backgrounds or controls.

Read guide ↗
02 / 08

Why relative luminance determines contrast

Text and background contrast uses relative luminance, not raw differences between HEX numbers.

Read guide ↗
03 / 08

Distinguish normal and large text thresholds

WCAG AA has different thresholds for different text sizes; rounded display values do not decide a pass.

Read guide ↗
04 / 08

Communicate meaning without color alone

Add text, shape or pattern when color conveys a state or instruction.

Read guide ↗
05 / 08

Check input boundaries, icons and essential graphics

Non-text contrast concerns objects carrying information, rather than every decoration.

Read guide ↗
06 / 08

Design a visible keyboard focus state

A palette does not end at the default state; keyboard navigation must remain visible.

Read guide ↗
07 / 08

Build palettes by role, not swatch count

Choose surfaces, text, borders and accents, then test the actual touching pairs.

Read guide ↗
08 / 08

Make a color review sheet before publishing

Record each color pair, its purpose, calculated result and visual review in one place.

Read guide ↗
